appraisal_events.evidence: "Sa mine grisâtre semblait éclairée par le reflet plombé d'un orage. Son essoufflement, qui ne se produisait, cet été encore, que quand M. Verdurin l'« engueulait », était maintenant constant."; "Pourquoi singulièrement ? demanda le baron, qui vit dans cet adverbe une critique."
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator depicts Saniette as worn down and chronically anxious (breathlessness once triggered only by M. Verdurin's scolding is now constant), and even his innocuous word choice draws suspicion from Charlus, so that Brichot must step in to defend him; the passage marks Saniette as socially fragile, even though Brichot's intervention partly rescues him.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Voyez-vous ça ! ça sort avec sa cousine, comme c'est pur ! »; « Mais nous ne vous demandons pas de comptes... vous avez très bon goût, elle est charmante votre cousine... On la regrettera ce soir. »; « vous êtes vert ; allons, entrons, vous prenez froid, vous avez mauvaise mine. »
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus teases the narrator with a knowing, faintly ironic jab about his 'cousine,' but then folds him into his own affectionate circle with praise and expressions of regret, and shows personal solicitude about his pallor; the narrator is staged as an included, favored young companion, with a light needling undertone.

appraisal_events.evidence: "il sentait que Bergotte n'était pas utilitaire comme les gens du monde et méritait mieux"; "il était été toute sa vie incapable d'une bonté suivie, mais désireux de faire plaisir, compréhensif, insensible au plaisir de donner une leçon"
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's account contrasts Bergotte favorably with worldly, utilitarian people: Bergotte recognized he was being used by Charlus yet bore no grudge, remaining generous, understanding, and free of the wish to moralize, a portrait that elevates his character even while noting his lack of sustained goodness.

status_effects.explanation: His visible physical decline and the ease with which Charlus suspects him of a slight underline his precarious, dependent standing among this company, only partly offset by Brichot's defense.
Despite a teasing undertone, Charlus's warmth, compliments, and personal concern stage the narrator as an included, favored participant in the baron's social sphere at this moment.
The narrator's account presents Bergotte as more genuine and generous than the socially utilitarian people around him, deserving of better treatment than he received.
